# SVD mathematics

## Basic definition

$$
A = U \Sigma V^{T}
  = \left[\vec u_1\; \vec u_2\; \cdots\; \vec u_n\right]
    \operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i)
    \left[\vec v_1\; \vec v_2\; \cdots\; \vec v_m\right]^{T}
$$ {#eq-svd}

- $A$ : data ($n \times m$)
- $U$ : left singular vectors, unitary ($U U^{T} = U^{T} U = I_{n \times n}$)
- $V$ : right singular vectors, unitary ($V V^{T} = V^{T} V = I_{m \times m}$)
- $\Sigma$ : singular values

## SVD properties : singular vectors are eigenvectors of correlation matrix
$$
A A^{T} = (U \Sigma V^{T}) (V \Sigma^{T} U^{T}) = U \Sigma^2 U^{T}
$$ {#eq-svd-aaT}
$$
A^{T} A = (V \Sigma^{T} U^{T}) (U \Sigma V^{T}) = V \Sigma^2 V^{T}
$$ {#eq-svd-aTa}

- $A^{T} A$ and $A A^{T}$ are symmetric, positive semi-definite matrices
- $U$ : eigenvectors of $A A^{T}$, with eigenvalues $\lambda_i = \sigma_i^2$
- $V$ : eigenvectors of $A^{T} A$, with eigenvalues $\lambda_i = \sigma_i^2$

::: footer
Properties of $A^{T}A$ / $AA^{T}$ :
[bsc-iitm.github.io — ATA and AAT](https://bsc-iitm.github.io/karthikt/notes/linear_algebra/ata_and_aat.html)
:::

## $A^{T}A$ and $AA^{T}$ : rank and nullspace

- **Symmetry** : $(A^{T}A)^{T} = A^{T}A$ and $(AA^{T})^{T} = AA^{T}$
- **Equal nullspaces** : $N(A) = N(A^{T}A)$ and $N(A^{T}) = N(AA^{T})$
- **Rank equality** :

$$
\operatorname{rank}(A^{T}A) = \operatorname{rank}(AA^{T}) = \operatorname{rank}(A) = r
$$ {#eq-rank-equality}

- **Invertibility** : $A^{T}A$ ($m \times m$) is invertible $\iff \operatorname{rank}(A) = m$
  (full column rank) — the condition behind the normal equations
  $\hat{\vec x} = (A^{T}A)^{-1}A^{T}\vec b$

::: footer
Properties of $A^{T}A$ / $AA^{T}$ :
[bsc-iitm.github.io — ATA and AAT](https://bsc-iitm.github.io/karthikt/notes/linear_algebra/ata_and_aat.html)
:::

## $A^{T}A$ and $AA^{T}$ : spectrum

- **Non-negative eigenvalues** : $\lambda \geq 0$ for both (positive semi-definite)
- **Shared spectrum** : $A^{T}A$ and $AA^{T}$ have the *same non-zero* eigenvalues
- **Count** : both have exactly $r = \operatorname{rank}(A)$ positive eigenvalues
- **Eigenvector correspondence** : if $(\lambda, \vec v)$ is an eigenpair of
  $A^{T}A$ with $\lambda > 0$, then $(\lambda, \vec u)$ is an eigenpair of $AA^{T}$ with

$$
\vec u = \frac{A \vec v}{\sqrt{\lambda}}
$$ {#eq-eigvec-correspondence}

With $\lambda_i = \sigma_i^2$ this is exactly $\vec u_i = A\vec v_i / \sigma_i$ — the
relation used on the next slide.

::: footer
Properties of $A^{T}A$ / $AA^{T}$ :
[bsc-iitm.github.io — ATA and AAT](https://bsc-iitm.github.io/karthikt/notes/linear_algebra/ata_and_aat.html)
:::

## SVD properties : fresh start

$$
A\vec v_i = \sigma_i \vec u_i
$$ {#eq-svd-fresh-start}

until...

$$
A\vec v_r = \sigma_r \vec u_r
$$ {#eq-svd-fresh-start-r}
- $r$ : rank of $A$, $\sigma_r > 0$, $\sigma_{r+1} = 0$
- economy SVD : $A = U_r \Sigma_r V_r^{T}$, with $U_r$ ($n \times r$), $\Sigma_r$ ($r \times r$), $V_r$ ($m \times r$)

## SVD properties : low-rank approximation

## SVD properties : singular vectors are orthogonal
$$
\vec u_i^{T} \vec u_j = 0
$$
$$
\left(\frac{A \vec v_i}{\sigma_i}\right)^{T}\left(\frac{A \vec v_j}{\sigma_j}\right)
= \frac{\vec v_i^{T} A^{T} A \vec v_j}{\sigma_i \sigma_j}
= \frac{\sigma_j^2 \, \vec v_i^{T} \vec v_j}{\sigma_i \sigma_j}
= 0 \quad (i \neq j)
$$ {#eq-svd-orthogonal}

using the eigenvalue equation $A^{T}A\vec v_j = \sigma_j^2 \vec v_j$ (next slide)
and $\vec v_i^{T}\vec v_j = 0$.

::: footer
Properties of $A^{T}A$ / $AA^{T}$ :
[bsc-iitm.github.io — ATA and AAT](https://bsc-iitm.github.io/karthikt/notes/linear_algebra/ata_and_aat.html)
:::

## The eigenvalue equation of $A^{T}A$

Starting from @eq-svd-aTa and right-multiplying by $V$, with $V^{T}V = I_{m \times m}$ :

$$
A^{T}A\,V = V \Sigma^2 V^{T} V = V \Sigma^2
$$ {#eq-ata-times-v}

Reading this column by column gives the **eigenvalue equation** :

$$
A^{T}A\,\vec v_i = \sigma_i^2 \, \vec v_i = \lambda_i \vec v_i
\qquad \Longleftrightarrow \qquad
\left(A^{T}A - \lambda_i I\right)\vec v_i = \vec 0
$$ {#eq-ata-eigen}

- $\vec v_i$ : right singular vector $=$ eigenvector of $A^{T}A$
- $\lambda_i = \sigma_i^2 \geq 0$ : eigenvalue, non-negative since $A^{T}A$ is
  positive semi-definite
- non-trivial solutions require $\det\!\left(A^{T}A - \lambda I\right) = 0$
- identically, $A A^{T}\vec u_i = \sigma_i^2 \vec u_i$ from @eq-svd-aaT

::: footer
Properties of $A^{T}A$ / $AA^{T}$ :
[bsc-iitm.github.io — ATA and AAT](https://bsc-iitm.github.io/karthikt/notes/linear_algebra/ata_and_aat.html)
:::

## Geometrical interpretation of SVD
- $V^T \vec y$ : rotate $\vec y$ into the singular vector basis
- $\Sigma V^T \vec y$ : scale the rotated vector by the singular values
- $U \Sigma V^T \vec y$ : rotate back into the original basis

# Rigidity coefficients

## Friedenwald $K$

Classic Friedenwald relation between pressure and volume change over one
cardiac cycle:

$$
K = \frac{\log_{10}(P_s / P_d)}{\Delta V}
$$ {#eq-friedenwald}

- $P_d$, $P_s$: diastolic / systolic IOP (mmHg), from OPA
- $\Delta V$: pulsatile volume change (µL), from the choroidal area change
  $\Delta A$ via a spherical-shell model

$$
\Delta V = \frac{4}{3}\pi\left[(R + \delta t)^3 - R^3\right] \, f_{cov}
$$ {#eq-friedenwald-dv}

with $R$ the vitreous-chamber radius (from axial length), $\delta t = \Delta A
/ w_{px} \cdot s_{axial}$ the mean axial thickness change, and $f_{cov}$ the
covered fraction of the sphere.

## Sayah *et al.* (2020) approximation

Alternative $k$ coefficient (mm$^{-3}$), derived from choroidal *thickness*
pulsatility $\Delta CT$ rather than area:

$$
\Delta V = \frac{\pi}{2} \left(AL \cdot f_{AL} + CT\right)^2 \Delta CT
$$ {#eq-sayah-dv}

$$
k = \frac{\ln\!\left(\dfrac{IOP + OPA}{IOP}\right)}{\Delta V}
$$ {#eq-sayah}

- $AL$: axial length (mm), $f_{AL} = 0.87$ an axial adjustment factor
- $CT$: baseline choroidal thickness (mm), $\Delta CT$: peak-to-peak
  pulsatile amplitude (mm)
- $IOP$, $OPA$: intraocular pressure and ocular pulse amplitude (mmHg)

# Understanding SVD : numerical tests
## SVD for temporal signals
$$ 
A = \begin{bmatrix}\vec x\; \vec y\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} x(t_1) & x(t_2) & \cdots & x(t_m) \\  y(t_1) & y(t_2) & \cdots & y(t_m) \end{bmatrix} 
$$

$$
A A^T = \begin{bmatrix} x(t_1) & x(t_2) & \cdots & x(t_m) \\  y(t_1) & y(t_2) & \cdots & y(t_m) \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x(t_1) & y(t_1) \\  x(t_2) & y(t_2) \\  \vdots & \vdots \\  x(t_m) & y(t_m) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \sum_{i=1}^{m} x^2(t_i) & \sum_{i=1}^{m} x(t_i)y(t_i) \\  \sum_{i=1}^{m} x(t_i)y(t_i) & \sum_{i=1}^{m} y^2(t_i) \end{bmatrix}
$$
$$
A^T A = \begin{bmatrix} x(t_1) & y(t_1) \\  x(t_2) & y(t_2) \\  \vdots & \vdots \\  x(t_m) & y(t_m) \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x(t_1) & x(t_2) & \cdots & x(t_m) \\  y(t_1) & y(t_2) & \cdots & y(t_m) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} x^2(t_1)+y^2(t_1) & x(t_1)x(t_2)+y(t_1)y(t_2) & \cdots & x(t_1)x(t_m)+y(t_1)y(t_m) \\  x(t_2)x(t_1)+y(t_2)y(t_1) & x^2(t_2)+y^2(t_2) & \cdots & x(t_2)x(t_m)+y(t_2)y(t_m) \\  \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\  x(t_m)x(t_1)+y(t_m)y(t_1) & x(t_m)x(t_2)+y(t_m)y(t_2) & \cdots & x^2(t_m)+y^2(t_m) \end{bmatrix}
$$

## SVD for temporal signals
$$ 
A = \begin{bmatrix} x(t_1) & x(t_2) & \cdots & x(t_m) \\  y(t_1) & y(t_2) & \cdots & y(t_m) \end{bmatrix} 
$$

\begin{align}
A^T A &=\begin{bmatrix} x^2(t_1)+y^2(t_1) & x(t_1)x(t_2)+y(t_1)y(t_2) & \cdots & x(t_1)x(t_m)+y(t_1)y(t_m) \\  x(t_2)x(t_1)+y(t_2)y(t_1) & x^2(t_2)+y^2(t_2) & \cdots & x(t_2)x(t_m)+y(t_2)y(t_m) \\  \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\  x(t_m)x(t_1)+y(t_m)y(t_1) & x(t_m)x(t_2)+y(t_m)y(t_2) & \cdots & x^2(t_m)+y^2(t_m) \end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix} x(t_1)\vec x + y(t_1)\vec y \\  x(t_2)\vec x + y(t_2)\vec y \\  \vdots \\  x(t_m)\vec x + y(t_m)\vec y \end{bmatrix} \\
&= \vec x^T \vec x + \vec y^T \vec y
\end{align}


## Eigenvalue equation of $A^{T}A$ for two signals

The previous slide is a sum of two **rank-1 outer products** :

$$
A^{T}A = \vec x^{T}\vec x + \vec y^{T}\vec y ,
\qquad
\vec x = \left[x(t_1)\; \cdots\; x(t_m)\right],\;
\vec y = \left[y(t_1)\; \cdots\; y(t_m)\right]
$$ {#eq-ata-outer}

so the eigenvalue equation $A^{T}A\,\vec v = \lambda \vec v$ reads

$$
\left(\vec x\,\vec v\right)\vec x^{T} + \left(\vec y\,\vec v\right)\vec y^{T}
= \lambda \, \vec v
$$ {#eq-ata-eigen-signals}

- for $\lambda \neq 0$, the left side lies in $\operatorname{span}\{\vec x^{T}, \vec y^{T}\}$
  $\Rightarrow$ **every eigenvector with $\lambda > 0$ is a combination of the two signals**
- hence only $r = \operatorname{rank}(A) \leq 2$ non-zero eigenvalues, and $m - r$ zero ones,
  whatever the number of time samples $m$

::: footer
Properties of $A^{T}A$ / $AA^{T}$ :
[bsc-iitm.github.io — ATA and AAT](https://bsc-iitm.github.io/karthikt/notes/linear_algebra/ata_and_aat.html)
:::

## Eigenvalue equation of $A^{T}A$ : closed form

Since $A^{T}A$ ($m \times m$) and $AA^{T}$ ($2 \times 2$) share their non-zero
eigenvalues, solve the small one. With

$$
S_{xx} = \sum_{i} x^2(t_i), \quad
S_{yy} = \sum_{i} y^2(t_i), \quad
S_{xy} = \sum_{i} x(t_i)\,y(t_i)
$$ {#eq-gram-entries}

the characteristic equation $\det\!\left(AA^{T} - \lambda I\right) = 0$ gives

$$
\lambda_{\pm} = \frac{S_{xx} + S_{yy}}{2}
  \pm \sqrt{\left(\frac{S_{xx} - S_{yy}}{2}\right)^{2} + S_{xy}^{2}}
$$ {#eq-lambda-closed-form}

- $\sigma_{\pm} = \sqrt{\lambda_{\pm}}$ : the two singular values of $A$
- $S_{xy} = 0$ (orthogonal signals) $\Rightarrow \lambda_{\pm} = S_{xx},\, S_{yy}$ — the
  singular vectors align with $\vec x$ and $\vec y$
- $\lambda_- = 0 \Leftrightarrow S_{xx}S_{yy} = S_{xy}^{2}$ : the two signals are
  proportional, $\operatorname{rank}(A) = 1$

::: footer
Properties of $A^{T}A$ / $AA^{T}$ :
[bsc-iitm.github.io — ATA and AAT](https://bsc-iitm.github.io/karthikt/notes/linear_algebra/ata_and_aat.html)
:::

## Eigenvalues of $AA^{T}$ for $k$ signals

With $k$ signals $\vec x, \vec y, \vec z, \vec w, \vec q, \vec p$ sampled at $m$ times,
$A$ is $k \times m$ and $AA^{T}$ is the $k \times k$ **Gram matrix** $S_{ab} = \sum_{t} a(t)\,b(t)$ :

$$
AA^{T} =
\begin{bmatrix}
S_{xx} & S_{xy} & S_{xz} & S_{xw} & S_{xq} & S_{xp} \\
S_{xy} & S_{yy} & S_{yz} & S_{yw} & S_{yq} & S_{yp} \\
S_{xz} & S_{yz} & S_{zz} & S_{zw} & S_{zq} & S_{zp} \\
S_{xw} & S_{yw} & S_{zw} & S_{ww} & S_{wq} & S_{wp} \\
S_{xq} & S_{yq} & S_{zq} & S_{wq} & S_{qq} & S_{qp} \\
S_{xp} & S_{yp} & S_{zp} & S_{wp} & S_{qp} & S_{pp}
\end{bmatrix}
$$ {#eq-gram-k}

$k = 3, 4, 5$ are the leading principal submatrices of this $k = 6$ case.
The eigenvalues are the roots of $\det\!\left(AA^{T} - \lambda I\right) = 0$, of degree $k$.

::: footer
Properties of $A^{T}A$ / $AA^{T}$ :
[bsc-iitm.github.io — ATA and AAT](https://bsc-iitm.github.io/karthikt/notes/linear_algebra/ata_and_aat.html)
:::

## Eigenvalues of $AA^{T}$ : what is actually listable

| $k$ | signals | $\det(AA^{T}-\lambda I)$ | closed form ? |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 2 | $x,y$ | quadratic | yes — @eq-lambda-closed-form |
| 3 | $x,y,z$ | cubic | yes — Cardano (next slide) |
| 4 | $+\,w$ | quartic | in principle (Ferrari), unusable in practice |
| 5 | $+\,q$ | quintic | **no** — Abel–Ruffini |
| 6 | $+\,p$ | sextic | **no** — Abel–Ruffini |

From $k \geq 5$ there is no general expression by radicals: the eigenvalues exist,
are real and $\geq 0$, but are only reachable **numerically**.

What *is* listable for every $k$ — the Vieta relations on the roots :

$$
\sum_{i} \lambda_i = \operatorname{tr}(AA^{T}) = \sum_{a} \|\vec a\|^{2},
\qquad
\prod_{i} \lambda_i = \det(AA^{T})
$$ {#eq-vieta}

- $e_j(\lambda_1 \ldots \lambda_k) =$ sum of the $j \times j$ principal minors of $AA^{T}$
- number of $\lambda_i > 0$ equals $\operatorname{rank}(A) \leq \min(k, m)$
- $\det(AA^{T}) = 0$ as soon as the signals are linearly dependent

::: footer
Properties of $A^{T}A$ / $AA^{T}$ :
[bsc-iitm.github.io — ATA and AAT](https://bsc-iitm.github.io/karthikt/notes/linear_algebra/ata_and_aat.html)
:::

## $k = 3$ signals : closed form

For the symmetric $3 \times 3$ Gram matrix of $\vec x, \vec y, \vec z$, with
$\bar q = \operatorname{tr}(AA^{T})/3$ and

$$
P = \sqrt{\frac{(S_{xx}-\bar q)^2 + (S_{yy}-\bar q)^2 + (S_{zz}-\bar q)^2
   + 2\left(S_{xy}^2 + S_{xz}^2 + S_{yz}^2\right)}{6}},
\qquad
B = \frac{AA^{T} - \bar q I}{P}
$$ {#eq-cardano-setup}

$$
\varphi = \frac{1}{3}\arccos\!\left(\frac{\det B}{2}\right),
\qquad
\lambda_{1,2,3} = \bar q + 2P \cos\!\left(\varphi + \frac{2\pi j}{3}\right),
\; j = 0, 1, 2
$$ {#eq-cardano}

The three cosines sum to zero, so $\sum_i \lambda_i = 3\bar q = \operatorname{tr}(AA^{T})$
as required by @eq-vieta.

::: footer
Properties of $A^{T}A$ / $AA^{T}$ :
[bsc-iitm.github.io — ATA and AAT](https://bsc-iitm.github.io/karthikt/notes/linear_algebra/ata_and_aat.html)
:::

## Phase-shifted sines : rank 2 for any $k$

The degree-$k$ obstacle disappears for the case at hand. Every
$a_i(t) = \sin(2\pi f t + \phi_i)$ expands on **two** basis signals only :

$$
a_i(t) = \cos\phi_i \, \underbrace{\sin(2\pi f t)}_{\vec s}
       + \sin\phi_i \, \underbrace{\cos(2\pi f t)}_{\vec c}
\quad \Longrightarrow \quad
A = \Phi \begin{bmatrix} \vec s \\ \vec c \end{bmatrix},
\;\; \Phi_{i} = \left[\cos\phi_i \;\; \sin\phi_i\right]
$$ {#eq-sine-factorization}

So $\operatorname{rank}(A) \leq 2$ and **$AA^{T}$ has only 2 non-zero eigenvalues
whatever $k = 3, 4, 5, 6$** — the other $k - 2$ are exactly zero. Over an integer
number of periods, $\vec s \vec c^{T} \simeq 0$ and $\|\vec s\|^2 = \|\vec c\|^2 = m/2$, giving

$$
\lambda_{\pm} = \frac{m}{4}\left(k \pm \left|\sum_{i=1}^{k} e^{\,2 i \phi_i}\right|\right)
$$ {#eq-sine-eigenvalues}

- phases spread uniformly over $[0, \pi)$ $\Rightarrow \sum_i e^{2i\phi_i} = 0$ and
  $\lambda_+ = \lambda_- = mk/4$ : degenerate, no preferred direction
- the more the phases cluster, the larger $\lambda_+ / \lambda_-$

::: footer
Properties of $A^{T}A$ / $AA^{T}$ :
[bsc-iitm.github.io — ATA and AAT](https://bsc-iitm.github.io/karthikt/notes/linear_algebra/ata_and_aat.html)
:::

## Simple phase shifted sine waves
$$
y_i(t) = \sin(2\pi f t + \phi_i)
$$ {#eq-phase-shifted-sine}
- $\phi_i = [0 \; \pi/4 \; \pi/2 \; 3\pi/4 \; \pi]$ : phase shifts

# Realistic simulations

## The concept : a ring that breathes

![](figures_simulation/concept_anneau.png){width=92%}

![](figures_simulation/concept_kymographe.png){width=86%}

::: {style="font-size:0.6em"}
A ring of radial gaussians — a synthetic choroid whose **features sit on its
edge** — inflating and deflating radially on a 1.0 → 1.3 Hz chirp, rendered on the
**real acquisition calibration** : 11.4 µm/px lateral, 3.9 µm/px axial, 17.9 Hz,
401 frames (22.4 s).

- pixels are **not square** : a ring that is circular in µm is an ellipse in the
  pixel grid — and the pixel grid is what the SVD works on
- the typical 6 µm peak-to-peak amplitude is **1.54 px axially** : the motion is
  **sub-pixel**, invisible frame by frame, and only shows up as an intensity
  modulation once the temporal mean is removed
:::

::: footer
`Astronauts/simulate_svd_radial_gaussians.py` — figures : `figures_simulation/`
:::

## Noise sources : jitter + image noise

![](figures_simulation/bruit_sources.png){width=88%}

::: {style="font-size:0.62em"}
Two residual-registration jitters and one image noise, injected before the
measurement chain (`PixelTraceSource` → `DecomposedTraceSource(svd)` →
`LombScargleRateEstimator` → `OptimizedSpectralCombination` → `HilbertPhaseEstimator`).

- **jitter $x$** — common to the whole frame : shifts the ring as a block ; on a
  fixed-column slice it reads as a spurious vertical motion of the edge
- **jitter $y$** — independent per A-scan : shreds the pattern, destroying spatial
  coherence between neighbouring A-scans without moving the ring as a whole
- **image noise** — greys out the red/blue alternation without deforming its
  geometry : it attacks contrast, not position
:::

::: footer
`Astronauts/simulate_svd_radial_gaussians.py` — figures : `figures_simulation/`
:::

## Measured image noise in the real data

![](figures_bruit_reel/bruit_reel_mesure.png){width=80%}

::: {style="font-size:0.62em"}
82 / 102 registered cubes (`SegmentationVariations`, 20 rejected for
$R^2 < 0.5$), each frame compared to its cube's temporal mean —
$\operatorname{Var}[I]$ binned against $\mu$.

- **the noise is not speckle** : $p = 0.54\;[0.32, 0.72]$ in $\operatorname{Var} = c\,\mu^{p}$,
  between additive (0) and Poisson (1), far from multiplicative speckle (2)
- **where the variance sits** : 38 % constant, 63 % $\propto \mu$, $-2\%$ $\propto \mu^2$ —
  the $\mu^2$ term is the *only* one the simulation models
- **no scalar `noise_level` fits both** : 0.19 seen through speckle vs 2.75 through
  the additive floor, a factor $\simeq 14$
- **6 % per-frame gain fluctuation** ($\mathrm{CV}$), global to the image and absent
  from the simulation ; residuals are heavier-tailed than $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, skew $-0.26$

Expected : exported B-scans are **log-compressed**, so multiplicative speckle
becomes additive.
:::

::: footer
`Astronauts/quantify_image_noise.py` — figure : `figures_bruit_reel/make_figure_bruit.py`
:::

## Results : one factor at a time

![](figures_simulation/resultats_phaseA.png){width=90%}

::: {style="font-size:0.62em"}
554 runs. *Detected* = `LombScargle` confidence high/medium **and** relative
frequency error $\leq 10\%$. Each panel varies one factor, the others held at the
value printed above it.

- **amplitude** : 100 % from 0.5 to 10 µm — but at zero noise *and* zero jitter,
  so this panel bounds nothing on its own
- **image noise** : 100 % up to $\times 5$ the realistic level, 70 % at $\times 8$ ;
  correlation with ground truth $1.00 \rightarrow 0.83$
- **jitter $x$ and $y$** : 100 % detection up to 4 px of either, at the typical
  6 µm amplitude ; correlation degrades gently to $\simeq 0.89$

Taken **one at a time**, none of these factors defeats the chain at a realistic
amplitude — the correlation erodes well before the detection does.
:::

## Methods — imposed pulse, noise and design

![](figures_simulation_complexe/methodes_design.png){width=94%}

::: {style="font-size:0.62em"}
- **imposed pulse** : a chirp sweeping **60 → 78 BPM** over the acquisition, so the
  signal is deliberately **non-stationary** — a fixed-frequency test would flatter
  the chain
- **design** : 5 amplitudes × 3 `jitter_x` × 3 `jitter_y` × **15 replicates**
  = **675 runs** (1015 with the 1-D sweeps ; 1 failed run in total)
- **image noise is a nuisance variable, drawn per run** (0.5 – 3.1 × the realistic
  level) rather than a controlled axis — it is averaged inside each cell, so every
  number below already integrates over a spread of noise
:::

`Astronauts/simulate_svd_radial_gaussians.py` — figures : `figures_simulation_complexe/`
:::

## Amplitude is the major determinant

| amplitude | runs | **detected** | corr. median [IQR] |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| 1 µm | 135 | **25 %** | 0.39 [0.05, 0.68] |
| 2 µm | 135 | **72 %** | 0.84 [0.58, 0.94] |
| 3 µm | 135 | **96 %** | 0.94 [0.84, 0.97] |
| 6 µm | 135 | **100 %** | 0.97 [0.95, 0.99] |
| 8 µm | 135 | **100 %** | 0.97 [0.96, 0.99] |

![](figures_simulation_complexe/amplitude_detection.png){width=72%}

::: {style="font-size:0.62em"}
Each row pools **all** jitter and noise conditions. Detection goes from 25 % to
100 % across the amplitude range — no other factor spans anything close to that.
The transition is sharp between **2 and 3 µm**.
:::

`Astronauts/simulate_svd_radial_gaussians.py` — figures : `figures_simulation_complexe/`

## The most critical jitter is in $y$

![](figures_simulation_complexe/jitter_xy.png){width=80%}

::: {style="font-size:0.62em"}
| σ (px) | detect. $j_x$ | detect. $j_y$ | corr. $j_x$ | corr. $j_y$ |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 | 98.7 % | 98.7 % | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| 1 | 94.7 % | **82.7 %** | 0.97 | 0.98 |
| 2 | 88.0 % | **69.3 %** | 0.91 | 0.88 |

At 2 px, jitter in $y$ costs **19 points of detection more** than jitter in $x$
(69 % vs 88 %) — each column moving on its own destroys the spatial coherence
between neighbouring A-scans, which is exactly what the SVD relies on.

Note the two metrics disagree at $\sigma = 1$ : $j_y$ already costs 12 points of
detection while its correlation is still 0.98. The pulse is still *there* — the
rate estimator just stops being confident about it.
:::

::: footer
`Astronauts/simulate_svd_radial_gaussians.py` — figures : `figures_simulation_complexe/`
:::

## Jitter in $x$ creates a spatial mode

![](figures_simulation_complexe/run_jx2_jy0.png){width=88%}

::: {style="font-size:0.62em"}
3 µm, $j_x = 2$ px, $j_y = 0$. **$v_1$ is a clean left–right dipole** — red on one
flank, blue on the other : the signature of the whole ring translating sideways.
A common-mode shift is coherent across the image, so the SVD gives it **its own
component**, well separated from the pulsation. Correlation stays at 0.94 and
confidence `high`.
:::

::: footer
`Astronauts/simulate_svd_radial_gaussians.py` — replicate closest to the cell median
:::

## Jitter in $y$ does not

![](figures_simulation_complexe/run_jx0_jy2.png){width=88%}

::: {style="font-size:0.62em"}
3 µm, $j_x = 0$, $j_y = 2$ px. **No dipole anywhere** : $v_1 \ldots v_5$ are
fragmented vertical striping. Because each A-scan moves independently, the
perturbation is *incoherent* and has no single spatial mode to occupy — it spreads
across many components instead. The aggregation is forced to keep **7** of them
(against 3 opposite), correlation falls to 0.88 and confidence drops to `medium`.

That is the mechanism behind the previous slide : $j_x$ is separable, $j_y$ is not.
:::

::: footer
`Astronauts/simulate_svd_radial_gaussians.py` — replicate closest to the cell median
:::

## Phase : a constant offset, not a filter dispersion {.scrollable}

![](figures_simulation_complexe/run_jx2_jy2_phase.png){width=100% .nostretch}

::: {style="font-size:0.6em"}
8 µm, $j_x = j_y = 2$ px. The measured Hilbert phase sits **+89° from the true
chirp phase** — but three checks say this is **not** a filtering artefact :

- the reconstructed pulse peaks at **lag 0** against ground truth (correlation
  0.948 at zero shift — no temporal delay at all)
- the offset is **±90° in every condition tested, including $j_x = j_y = 0$ and
  zero noise** — it is not caused by the degradations
- it **does not drift** with the chirp ($-1.7°$ from start to end, against a $7°$
  scatter) ; a filter-induced shift would be frequency-dependent

$\pm 90°$ is the quadrature convention of the analytic signal — for $x = \sin\theta$
the Hilbert phase is $\theta - 90°$, and the arbitrary SVD sign flips it. It is a
**constant, removable offset**, not dispersion.

What *is* degraded : the instantaneous rate is unbiased (median error $0.1$ BPM)
but its spread widens with degradation (IQR $0.4 \rightarrow 2.0$ BPM), and the
**Hilbert edge artefacts** at $t = 0$ and $t = 22$ s are large.
:::

`Astronauts/simulate_svd_radial_gaussians.py` — replicate closest to the cell median
